Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the model latency and control features look promising for our patient-summary workflow. Before we can finalize timelines with procurement, two quick asks so our legal and procurement teams can reconcile:  

1) MAP / evaluation plan: We want to lock in a 6-week evaluation across staging and pilot with clearly defined milestones (data ingest, 1:1 clinical pilot, user feedback loop). Could you share a short MAP that maps milestones to commercial triggers (discounts/commits)?

2) Overage and burst pricing during ramp: Our security team wants to understand how bursts above committed throughput are invoiced during the 6-week ramp. Is there a soft cap we can set? Any possibility of a limited grace credit for unexpected traffic during pilot?

Procurement cc'd — they want to know if we can make signature & procurement steps happen before the pilot ends (we are aiming to close by 2025-12-10).

Thanks,
Lisa

Hi Lisa — great to hear. I pulled together a short MAP and an initial rate-card summary for the pilot. Attaching the MAP draft (RDW-Acme_MAP_DRAFT_v1.pdf) and a short rate-card extract. High-level answers up front:  

- MAP: 6-week evaluation split into three milestones: (1) Week 1–2: data onboarding & baseline tests; (2) Week 3–4: 1:1 clinician pilot (up to 50 concurrent users); (3) Week 5–6: expanded pilot & quality validation. Each milestone has a pass/fail checkpoint and a documented prompt set. If Milestone 2 passes, a 10% committed-month discount becomes available when you convert to a reserved capacity commit.

- Overage / burst during ramp: We provide automatic burst capacity above the committed baseline up to 2x for short windows (under 6 minutes) at a premium per-token rate. For pilot periods we can set a soft cap (alerts at 80% and hard throttle at 250% of baseline unless you opt-out). For this pilot, we can offer one-time grace coverage of up to $2,000 in unexpected overage charges (applied as credit) provided the burst pattern is non-continuous and you notify us within 48 hours.

I've looped in Ben (pricing) to confirm numbers and any exceptions for procurement. If this aligns, I'll drop the MAP into the shared drive and create a DocuSign SOW template with the staged-commit language.

Best,
Priyom

--
Priyom Das

Thanks Priyom — adding some concrete pricing bullets and the rate-card pointer (attached: rate_card-exec-summary-2025.xlsx). Quick notes:  

- Baseline & commit: For the pilot we recommend a small reserved slab: 200k tokens/day baseline (this keeps latency SLOs consistent). If you convert to a monthly commit within 10 days after Milestone 2 pass, you get the staged discount structure we discussed (10% on the first 3 months, then re-evaluate).

- Overage / burst rates: Overage is billed at 3x the per-token baseline rate for the excess tokens above the baseline up to the hard cap; sustained excess (>72 hours at >120% baseline) triggers a review and possible reclassification to a higher slab. Short bursts (< 6 minutes) are billed at 1.5x. We can include threshold alerts in console and automatic webhook notifications for procurement.

- Soft cap mechanics: We can configure a rolling 7-day soft cap (alerts at 80%/95%) and a separate pilot hard cap that you can set per environment. For the evaluation we propose pilot hard cap = 500k tokens/day. If you want a stricter procurement-friendly approach, we can codify a hard spend ceiling and split overage exposure between Redwood and Acme for the first 30 days (example: Redwood covers first $2k as credit, Acme covers subsequent overage).

Action items: Priyom — can you confirm the exact commit language we should push into the SOW? Lisa / procurement — does split exposure and a hard spend ceiling sound acceptable?

-Ben

Ben Carter

1) They want the split-exposure example written into the SOW (exact wording) and a firm hard spend ceiling (we suggest $7,500 for the pilot).  
2) Legal asked if the grace credit can be expanded to include one instance of a higher burst (up to $5k) if triggered by a platform incident on Redwood's side (e.g., misrouted traffic or misconfigured autoscale).

Also — timeline check: we think procurement can sign if the SOW and MAP are delivered by EOD Thu (2025-12-04) and DocuSign link is available for countersignature the same day. Is that feasible? Our goal is to be fully contracted before end of pilot (target close 2025-12-10).

Thanks,
Lisa

Summary of agreed commercial points for pilot (to be captured in the SOW):
